rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act - Just Cause Eviction
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential property for 12 months (or 24 months if an adult tenant is added before 24 months), a landlord may not terminate the tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in the written notice.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential real property after 12 months of continuous occupancy, excluding hotels, hospitals, dormitories, certain owner-occupied units, units built within the previous 15 years, and deed-restricted affordable housing.
coverage.owner_condition: Exempts certain single-family owner-occupied residences and certain owner-occupied duplexes.

rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotels; non-profit hospitals, religious facilities, and care facilities; school dormitories; units sharing bathroom/kitchen with owner; single-family owner-occupied residences renting no more than two units/bedrooms; certain owner-occupied duplexes; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; certain separately alienable properties owned by natural persons; deed-restricted affordable housing.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
